subject: Records sovereignty and extract scenarios — Q&A
messages:
From: Alice Johansson <alice@finvero.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: security@finvero.com
Date: Wed, 11 Oct 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on records residency & extracts for audit handback

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. We have two upcoming compliance gates (internal audit + external regulator spot-check) and the auditors are asking for a clear description of:

• Where tenant-level audit & access traces can be exported to (S3 destination, for example)
• Whether we can request a snapshot that includes identity metadata (user id, role) plus the raw request/response hashes
• The retention window options and whether exported snapshots can be sliced by date ranges and jurisdictions

Attached is a simple matrix that our legal team started (audit_handback_matrix.xlsx). Can you confirm what Redwood can produce without a formal export job vs what requires a formal handback? Also flag any residency constraints we should be aware of — specifically: can exports for our EU customers be delivered to an EU S3 bucket?

Appreciate a short summary we can share with our auditors.

Best,
Alice
Alice Johansson
Head of Compliance
Finvero Financial

Attachment: audit_handback_matrix.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Johansson <alice@finvero.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Oct 2028 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on records residency & extracts for audit handback

Hi Alice —

Thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, details below:

1) Destinations: Yes — for both hosted and Dedicated customers we can deliver audit/access trace exports to customer-owned S3 buckets (us/eu/apac) or to an SFTP endpoint. For Private deployments we can hand off to your internal storage.

2) Snapshot contents: We can produce time-sliced snapshots that include timestamped event records, request metadata, and associated identity identifiers (ID, role). We do NOT include full customer prompt/response text unless there is an explicit legal/data request (we treat those as separate data extracts with elevated review).

3) Residency constraints: Exports targeted to an EU S3 bucket remain within the EU egress path when the tenant is region-bound and the storage bucket is EU-located. Cross-border delivery requires a signed agreement and an export job flagged for cross‑region handoff (adds 48–72h).

Details:
• Ad-hoc vs formal: Lightweight ad-hoc exports (last 7/30/90 days) can be initiated via Console by an Admin and are processed via our standard export pipeline (no legal sign-off). Large handbacks or full-tenant history (multi-year) are initiated through our Support/Legal export playbook and require an export request form + PoA for delivery.

• Slicing: We support arbitrary date-range slicing and can apply jurisdiction tags if your tenant has region labels. If you need per-user filters, include the user IDs in the request; we will validate access controls before export.

• Identity metadata: We include user identifiers and roles; we do not automatically include hashed tokens or decrypted secrets. If you need expanded identity joins (e.g., mapping to your internal SSO IDs), we can include a mapping file as an additional artifact if you supply the mapping table.

Looping in Karthik (serving infra) and Naomi (privacy/legal) to confirm SLA and any extra documentation we should provide for auditors.

Thanks — happy to make this a short one-pager for your auditors.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success (Security & Compliance)
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Alice Johansson <alice@finvero.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Oct 2028 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on records residency & extracts for audit handback

Hi Alice — quick technical clarifications from infra:

• Formats & integrity: Exports are delivered as compressed newline-delimited JSON (ndjson) by default, plus an index CSV. Each delivery includes checksums (sha256) and a signed manifest.

• Redaction rules: By default we apply PII redaction for fields flagged in the tenant's privacy profile. If you request identity fields, we can disable redaction for those fields for the export job after a recorded approval.

• Transfer mechanics: For EU-target buckets we route traffic via our EU edge and the data will not transit US egress points (when tenant is EU-regioned). For cross-region handoffs we stage in an encrypted temporary container, perform the transfer, then tombstone the staged copy according to the agreed TTL.

• Timing & throughput: Small ad-hoc slices (<=30 days) typically complete within 4–8 hours. Full-tenant handbacks (multi-year) depend on size — expect 2–10 days; we will provide a job ETA and progress logs.

If you want, we can provide a sample ndjson extract (synthetic) and the manifest so auditors can see the shape.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Alice —

Following up after internal checks with Naomi:

• For your auditors, the short blurb you can share: Redwood can deliver tenant audit and access traces to customer-owned storage within the same region. Export deliveries include a signed manifest, checksums, and configurable redaction settings. Cross-border exports are supported but require a signed export agreement and typically add 48–72 hours to delivery.

• We attached a sample export manifest and the residency map to this thread (see data_residency_map.pdf).

Next steps I suggest:
1) Confirm which tenants (IDs) you want included and the date range.
2) Tell us destination details (S3 bucket ARN or SFTP endpoint) and your preferred encryption key (if using customer-managed CMK).
3) If you need per-user unredacted identity fields, please send the PoA and confirmation from your security team so we can toggle the field whitelist.

Once we have that we can spin up the ad-hoc 90-day slice (or schedule a full-handback) and share a sample manifest.

Would you like me to draft the one-page summary for auditors?

Thanks,
—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success (Security & Compliance)
Redwood Inference
